definitions.meaning: a minor graze or nick on the skin
in golf a ... player plays off a handicap of zero

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a minor injury as being no obstacle at all.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf a player with no handicap is said to play off scratch.
explanation.definitionFit: A scratch is a slight wound, and a scratch golfer has a zero handicap.

clue.text: Upset? Depends on how big-headed one is!

definitions.meaning: to overturn, as a boat does when it tips over

definitions.text: Depends on how big-headed one is!
definitions.meaning: taken literally, the measurement of a hat depends on the size of the head

explanation.surface: A jibe that someone's ego determines how easily they are upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big-headed' suggests conceit, but here it simply means having a large head, which needs a larger hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Boats overturn when they capsize; read as two words, cap size is hat measurement.

definitions.meaning: further forward, in front of others
a head is the head teacher of a school

explanation.surface: Asks whether a teacher is further on than the pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as A HEAD, the answer names a head teacher; 'as' just links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in front or further on is being ahead; a head teacher runs a school.

indicators.note: the word for favourite is placed in the middle of the word for enter

parts.note: to enter is to come in
a favourite, such as a teacher's favourite, is a pet

explanation.surface: Putting a favourite horse into a race.
explanation.definitionFit: To contest a prize is to vie or compete for it.

parts.note: spectacles are a pair of lenses, so a single one worn in one eye is a singular spectacle

explanation.surface: Something remarkable to behold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular spectacle' reads as an extraordinary sight, but means one lens rather than a pair of glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeglass worn over a single eye is literally one of a pair of spectacles.

indicators.note: letters in trouble are thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Workers giving their struggling managers a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in difficulty' rearranges BOSSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To obsess someone is to preoccupy and torment their mind.

indicators.note: the wines are made ready in a fresh form, so their letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A diner told the white wine is off is offered rosé instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided' rearranges WHITE and ROSE; the accent on the rosé is ignored. 'Provided' looks like 'on condition that', pairing with 'if not'.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise means or else, in other circumstances, a synonym of if not.

parts.note: the bay tree's leaves were woven into wreaths to crown victors

explanation.surface: Coastal inlets where some triumph was won.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bays' suggests coastal inlets, but means bay trees, whose leaves crowned winners.
explanation.definitionFit: Wreaths of bay leaves were awarded as tokens of triumph, hence resting on one's honours.

parts.note: a road crossing painted with black and white bars that walkers use

explanation.surface: Something walkers are forbidden to enter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barred' suggests forbidden, but means striped: a British road crossing painted in black and white stripes, where pedestrians have priority.
explanation.definitionFit: A striped road crossing for walkers is named after the striped African animal.

clue.text: Primate seen around Sunday in church

indicators.note: the ape is seen surrounding the abbreviation, placed on both sides of it

explanation.surface: A monkey spotted at a Sunday church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded recess at the east end of a church building, found within it.

indicators.note: the words break open so their letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: A water pipe that splits every summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bursts' rearranges EACH SUMMER; the water-pipe picture hides a tobacco pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A meerschaum is a tobacco pipe with a bowl carved from white clay mineral.

explanation.surface: Someone takes part in a game but plays dishonestly.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddle means play the violin and, informally, to swindle or falsify.

definitions.meaning: makes a booking, as of seats or a table

explanation.surface: A list of money saved and books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'books' looks like a noun but is the verb, to make a booking.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserves are funds held back, and reserves also means books in advance.

clue.text: Home one left when decree nisi brought round

indicators.note: the remaining letters are turned about into a new order
the letter for one departs from the phrase

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone leaves the family home after a divorce decree nisi is delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: A decree nisi is the provisional divorce order in English law. Removing one I ('left') from DECREE NISI leaves DECREENSI; 'brought round' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is the place where someone lives, their house or dwelling.

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of their places and laid down in another order

explanation.surface: Advice to withdraw one's pension investments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take out' rearranges ANNUITIES; it reads as a financial instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To insinuate is to suggest indirectly, to imply or hint.

definitions.meaning: a top-class honours degree at a British university

explanation.surface: A degree awarded to someone heading a department.
explanation.walkthrough: A British honours degree is classed first, upper second, lower second or third.
explanation.definitionFit: A first is the top class of degree; first also means leading or foremost.

clue.text: Resort to sergeant major to get fit

parts.note: a spa is a health resort
SM is the military abbreviation for sergeant major

explanation.surface: A soldier is sent to a health resort to get back in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like healthy but is a noun, a sudden seizure.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit is a sudden convulsion or seizure, the same as a muscular spasm.

parts.note: to put forward a marriage, asking someone to wed

explanation.surface: Handing someone a match to light a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests a light or a game but means a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose is to ask for someone's hand in marriage.

clue.text: Fell in love but became discouraged

explanation.surface: A romance that started well but ended in despair.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing your heart to someone is falling for them; losing heart is giving up hope.

clue.text: A unit is ordered to somewhere in North Africa

indicators.note: the letters are told to fall into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A military unit is posted to North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is ordered' rearranges A UNIT IS; the surface reads as a posting order.
explanation.definitionFit: A country on the Mediterranean coast of North Africa, between Algeria and Libya.

indicators.note: the list holds the zero within it

parts.note: a roll, as in a roll call, is a roster or list of names

explanation.surface: A bread roll filled only with chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll' and 'chicken' suggest a sandwich; 'chicken' is the bird itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel, a male domestic chicken.

clue.text: Holidays that fall in the autumn

definitions.meaning: foliage that drops from trees in the autumn

explanation.surface: Holidays that are taken in the autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' suggests holidays falling on dates, but means the leaves dropping off trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave is time off, so plural leaves are holidays; trees shed their leaves in the autumn.

clue.text: They may lead to quick ducks for any batsmen

definitions.text: They may lead to quick ducks for any batsmen

parts.words: They may lead to quick ducks for any batsmen
parts.note: in cricket a short-pitched ball that rears up makes batsmen duck, and can also get them out for a duck, zero runs

explanation.surface: Something causing a batsman to be out quickly for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero; a fast bowler's short, rising delivery also makes batsmen duck their heads.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-pitched fast deliveries in cricket that rear up towards the batsman's head.

clue.text: He brought fresh weight to laws of motion

definitions.text: He brought fresh weight to laws of motion

parts.note: a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A scientist who gave new force to the laws of motion.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the physicist who formulated the three laws of motion, while 'fresh' and 'weight' build the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton, the English physicist, set out the three laws of motion.

parts.note: the middle of the three measurements of bust, middle and hips

explanation.surface: An important office where statistics are compiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vital statistics' are a person's bust, waist and hip measurements; the centre of the three is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle of the body, the second of the three figure measurements.

indicators.note: the words are cooked up and their letters come out mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Pastries baked in a vaulted oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges OVEN VAULTS, fitting the baking picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Small round cases of puff pastry filled with a savoury mixture.

clue.text: I return to a trivial item

indicators.note: the little word is turned back to front

explanation.surface: Someone goes back to a minor matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses TO to give OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota, the smallest Greek letter, means a tiny amount or trifle.

explanation.surface: A loss, or perhaps the very opposite of one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite the opposite' seems to mean victory, but is itself the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverse is a setback or defeat; the reverse is the contrary.

clue.text: Army set out to gain control

indicators.note: the troops are set out in a new formation, so their letters change places

explanation.surface: Troops are deployed to take command of a region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ARMY SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastery is command or domination over something.
